question: Ticket 380d524e6e9c says 'Linux launcher unchanged; no thin platform shell created; explicitly excluded from this slice', but outline 5.4.3.8.1 reads "In front of it sits a thin platform shell (a shell script on Linux, cairn.cmd or cairn.ps1 on Windows) with enough brains to fall over to Rescue (6.5) when it can't find Cairn's Python, or Python throws, or anything else stops the launcher. The failure throws a trouble ticket (3.4.3), and the ticket is Rescue's "read this" (6.5.3.5); a repeat increments that ticket's counter. Rescue's prompt says: at the end of proving the fix, check for more errors, to clear or fix as appropriate. WHY: trouble has to be able to report when nothing else can (2.3.7.1.3)." (Outline 5.4.3.8.1 requires 'a thin platform shell (a shell script on Linux, cairn.cmd or cairn.ps1 on Windows)' in front of the Python launcher on both platforms. The ticket implements cairn.cmd for Windows but deliberately omits the thin shell script for Linux, leaving bin/cairn as a direct bash launcher instead of a shell wrapping a Python dispatcher.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. The shell-front fallover to Rescue and the trouble ticket (5.4.3.8.1-3) is cast as its own ticket ddc9957704d2, owned by the recovery charter, depends on 380d524e6e9c. 380d524e6e9c stays the dispatcher slice.
